140  THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE

by the state domain for universities was decided, and in addition to other old grants of land and appropriate revenues which have given millions of dollars in support of our state university. The latter has been endowed by gifts of land domain for the University of Texas. The latter has been endowed by gifts from the permanent fund derived from public lands to the public-school system with a university of the first class at its head with appropriate revenues. Both the A. and M. College was made a "branch of the University of Texas." Both were provided with various resources for establishing other colleges such as normals (as they were then called) in various parts of the state, together with a university of the highest type. The appropriation of "one tenth" referred to was given to the general public-school system and all the poll taxes of male teachers in the public school of Texas. Both were provided with various resources for establishing other colleges such as normals in various parts of the state, and becoming permanently endowed. The land for state universities by the Constitution of 1876 was set aside, and all the poll taxes of male teachers in the public school of Texas were given. All were provided with adequate resources for establishing other colleges such as normals (as they were then called) in various parts of the state, and becoming permanently established.

The wisdom and foresight of those men are shown in that we can't burn them away, and the solid intangible rewards they have preserved are most indelible in our people's memories. These men are shown as the college land can't be sold or used, if sold, the money must come from the state, not from the private resources of top down; but from the people, not from the state supported institutions, to meet educational measures.
notes: Page 140 of printed text. Discusses Texas educational policy, land grants, and the University of Texas system.
